title: Edit Distance
corePattern: 2D Dynamic Programming on Strings - Alignment DP
interviewTips: Clarify allowed operations: insert, delete, replace each cost 1, and ask if operations are on word1 to word2 or either direction.
Trade-off: 2D DP is easiest to explain and reconstruct path, 1D DP is optimal for memory; mention only needing previous row.
Edge-case tip: handle empty strings first, and discuss swapping to make DP width equal to shorter string for O(min(m,n)) space.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Recursion
approaches.intuition: Compare first unmatched characters of suffixes. If equal, skip both with no cost. If different, try all three operations: delete from word1, insert into word1, replace, each costs 1 plus best of remainder. This explores all edit sequences.
approaches.theory: Define f(i,j) as edit distance of suffixes word1[i:] and word2[j:]. Base: if i==m return n-j (insert rest), if j==n return m-i (delete rest). Transition: if word1[i]==word2[j] then f(i+1,j+1), else 1+min(f(i+1,j), f(i,j+1), f(i+1,j+1)). Recursion branches up to 3 ways, leading to exponential overlapping subproblems.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each mismatched state branches into 3 calls (insert, delete, replace). In worst case with all chars different, recursion tree size is exponential in m+n. No memoization so same (i,j) recomputed many times.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion stack depth at most m+n along any path, no extra memo table.

steps: dfs(0,0): h vs r mismatch -> try delete h, insert r, replace h->r
Best path is replace/insert/delete exploration, e.g., horse -> rorse (replace h) -> rose (delete r) -> ros (delete e)
Equal chars cause free diagonal moves without cost
Minimum over all branches evaluates to 3

edgeCases: One or both strings empty: answer is length of other string
Identical strings: answer 0 via always-equal fast path
Single char vs long string: TLE due to exponential blowup, motivates memoization

approaches.name: Approach 2: Top-Down DP with Memoization
approaches.intuition: Same recursion as brute force but cache result of each (i,j) pair. Number of distinct states is only (m+1)*(n+1), so each is computed once.
approaches.theory: Overlapping subproblems: many paths reach same (i,j). Store f(i,j) in memo table initialized to -1/unvisited. On entry check memo, on exit save. Correctness follows from optimal substructure: optimal edit for prefixes/suffixes composes from optimal edits of smaller suffixes plus one operation. Converts exponential recursion to polynomial DAG traversal.

timeComplexity.explanation: There are (m+1)*(n+1) states, each does O(1) work excluding recursive calls due to memo hit. So total time linear in state count.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Memo table of size (m+1)*(n+1) plus recursion stack O(m+n) in worst case.

steps: dfs(0,0) mismatch -> needs dfs(1,0), dfs(0,1), dfs(1,1)
Memo ensures dfs(2,1) etc. reached via multiple paths computed once
Filled bottom-up via recursion unwinding yields 3

edgeCases: Empty string: base case returns immediately without table fill
Long strings up to 500: recursion depth up to 1000 may overflow in C++/Java, consider iterative
All same chars: linear diagonal chain, memo still O(m*n) worst but fast path

approaches.name: Approach 3: Bottom-Up DP with Space Optimization
approaches.intuition: Build dp for prefixes: dp[i][j] is distance between first i chars of word1 and first j chars of word2. If last chars equal, inherit diagonal; else take 1 plus best of delete, insert, replace. Only previous row needed, so compress to 1D.
approaches.theory: Prefix optimal substructure mirrors suffix version. Initialization: dp[i][0]=i (delete all), dp[0][j]=j (insert all). Recurrence: if word1[i-1]==word2[j-1] then dp[i][j]=dp[i-1][j-1] else dp[i][j]=1+min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) corresponding to delete, insert, replace. Iterate i=1..m, j=1..n. Space optimization keeps prev and curr rows; swapping to make n=min(m,n) gives O(min(m,n)) memory. Time remains O(m*n).

timeComplexity.explanation: Double loop over m rows and n columns, each cell O(1). Optimal for this problem as all prefix pairs may be needed.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two 1D arrays of length min(m,n)+1 are kept (previous row and current row). Swapping ensures width is the shorter string.

edgeCases: Empty word: loop skipped, returns prev[n] which is other length
word1 shorter than word2: swap ensures minimal memory without changing answer (distance symmetric)
Identical strings: diagonal propagation yields 0, no overflow as max value m+n <= 1000 fits int
